source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα μεγάλης φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard a loud voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels: Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of the God into the earth.

en.L: And I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of God on the earth."
en.B: I heard a great voice speak from the temple to the seven angels: "Go and empty the seven bowls of God's fury onto the earth."
en.R: Then I heard a loud voice from the temple. It said to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth."

fr.L: Et j’entendis une voix forte [venant] du temple, qui disait aux sept anges : « Allez et versez sur la terre les sept coupes de la fureur de Dieu. »
fr.B: J’entendis une grande voix, venant du temple, dire aux sept anges : « Allez vider sur la terre les sept coupes de la fureur de Dieu. »
fr.R: Puis j’ai entendu une voix forte qui venait du temple. Elle a dit aux sept anges : « Allez verser sur la terre les sept coupes de la colère de Dieu. »

sw.L: Na nikasikia sauti kubwa kutoka katika hekalu ikiwaambia wale malaika saba, "Nendeni mkayamimine mabakuli saba ya hasira kali ya Mungu juu ya dunia."
sw.B: Nikasikia sauti kubwa kutoka hekaluni ikiwaambia wale malaika saba: "Nendeni mkayamwage mabakuli saba ya hasira kali ya Mungu juu ya dunia."
sw.R: Kisha nikasikia sauti kubwa kutoka hekaluni. Iliwaambia wale malaika saba, "Nendeni mkamimine juu ya dunia mabakuli saba yaliyojaa hasira kali ya Mungu."

es.L: Y oí una gran voz desde el templo que decía a los siete ángeles: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:derramen|derramad}} sobre la tierra las siete copas del furor de Dios».
es.B: Oí una gran voz que, desde el templo, decía a los siete ángeles: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:derramen|derramad}} sobre la tierra las siete copas del furor de Dios».
es.R: Luego oí una voz fuerte que salía del templo. Decía a los siete ángeles: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:derramen|derramad}} sobre la tierra las siete copas de la ira de Dios».

decisions.choice: a voice from the temple: God's own command
decisions.reason: No one could enter the temple until the plagues were done (15:8), so the voice from inside it is most likely God's.

decisions.choice: pouring out wrath: the prophets' language
decisions.reason: "Pour out your wrath on the nations" (Psalm 79:6; compare Jeremiah 10:25; Zephaniah 3:8). The bowls of chapter 15 are now poured.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R): "j’entendis" / "j’ai entendu"; the historic present of 16:21 kept at Literal ("descend")
decisions.reason: John tells what he saw and heard; the passé simple is the tense of careful written narrative, the passé composé the tense Readable uses throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the whole chapter.
As the English: Balanced says "vider sa coupe" so that the seven pourings do not repeat one phrase; "verser" is the plain word for pouring out the bowl at Literal and Readable.

Revelation sets two words for God's anger side by side (16:19). Swahili keeps them apart: "hasira kali" (fierce anger) for the first, which fills the bowls, and "ghadhabu" (wrath) for the second, as in 6:16-17.

Swahili has two verbs for pouring out a liquid: "kumimina" and "kumwaga" (to empty out, to spill). Balanced uses "kumwaga" for the angels emptying their bowls, as the English Balanced says "emptied"; Literal and Readable say "kumimina". The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: derramar (every level, for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: Spanish "derramar" is both the ordinary verb for pouring a liquid out and the prophets' word for pouring out wrath, so it serves every level; the English Balanced "emptied" has no need of a separate Spanish word.

decisions.choice: el furor de Dios (L, B); la ira de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in 14:10 and 15:7, "furor" renders the word for God's burning anger at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the plainer "ira".

source.text: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And went away the first and poured out the bowl of him into the earth, and came a sore bad and evil on the men the [ones] having the mark of the beast and those worshiping the image of it.

en.L: And the first went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and a bad and evil sore came on the {{gender:people|men}} who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.
en.B: The first angel went off and emptied his bowl on the earth, and foul, painful sores came on the {{gender:people|men}} who bore the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.
en.R: The first angel went and poured out his bowl on the land. Then terrible, painful sores broke out on the {{gender:people|men}} who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its statue.

fr.L: Et le premier s’en alla et versa sa coupe sur la terre, et un ulcère mauvais et pernicieux vint sur les {{gender:humains|hommes}} qui avaient la marque de la bête et qui adoraient son image.
fr.B: Le premier ange partit et vida sa coupe sur la terre ; et de mauvais ulcères, douloureux, frappèrent les {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui portaient la marque de la bête et adoraient son image.
fr.R: Le premier ange est parti et a versé sa coupe sur le pays. Alors des plaies terribles et douloureuses sont apparues sur les {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui avaient la marque de la bête et qui adoraient sa statue.

sw.L: Na wa kwanza akaenda, akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya dunia, na kukatokea jipu baya na ovu juu ya watu wenye chapa ya mnyama na wanaoisujudia sanamu yake.
sw.B: Malaika wa kwanza akaenda, akalimwaga bakuli lake juu ya dunia, na majipu mabaya yenye maumivu yakawapata watu waliokuwa na chapa ya mnyama na walioisujudia sanamu yake.
sw.R: Malaika wa kwanza alikwenda, akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya nchi. Ndipo majipu mabaya yenye maumivu makali yakawatokea watu wote waliokuwa na alama ya mnyama na walioiabudu sanamu yake.

es.L: Y fue el primero y derramó su copa sobre la tierra, y vino una llaga mala y maligna sobre {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que tenían la marca de la bestia y que adoraban su imagen.
es.B: El primer ángel fue y derramó su copa sobre la tierra, y a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que llevaban la marca de la bestia y adoraban su imagen les salieron llagas repugnantes y dolorosas.
es.R: El primer ángel fue y derramó su copa sobre la tierra. Entonces a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que tenían la marca de la bestia y adoraban su estatua les salieron llagas terribles y dolorosas.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: sores
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 9:9-11; compare Deuteronomy 28:35). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: only on those with the beast's mark
decisions.reason: The sores strike those who took the mark and worshiped the image (13:16-17; 14:9-11). The mark they took in their flesh brings a wound in their flesh.
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

decisions.choice: {{gender:humains|hommes}} (L); {{gender:gens|hommes}} (B, R) for the generic word (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: Where the English has {{gender:people|men}}, French chooses between the traditional "hommes" and an inclusive noun. Literal says "humains", the closest to the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "gens", the natural word for the people struck. Both are masculine plural, so no agreeing word changes.

decisions.choice: chapa ya mnyama (L, B), alama ya mnyama (R); sanamu yake
decisions.reason: "Mnyama" (beast) for the creature of chapter 13; its mark is "chapa" (a brand of ownership) at Literal and Balanced and the plain "alama" at Readable, as in 13:16-17 and 14:9-11, the same in 19:20 and 20:4; "sanamu" for its image.

alternatives: a gender span, as in the English
decisions.reason: "Watu" (people) already includes men and women, so the English span "people|men" has no Swahili counterpart; the same through the chapter.

The word is the one used for the boils of the Egyptian plague; "llaga" is the everyday Spanish word for an open sore. Literal keeps the singular and the Greek pair "mala y maligna"; Balanced and Readable use the plural and say what the sores were like.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ, καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And the second poured out the bowl of him into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead [one], and every soul of life died, the things in the sea.

en.L: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead [person], and every living soul died, the things in the sea.
en.B: When the second angel emptied his bowl into the sea, it became like the blood of a corpse, and everything that lived in the sea died.
en.R: The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea. The sea turned into blood like the blood of a dead body. Every living thing in the sea died.

fr.L: Et le deuxième versa sa coupe dans la mer, et elle devint du sang comme celui d’un mort, et toute âme vivante mourut, ce qui [était] dans la mer.
fr.B: Quand le deuxième ange vida sa coupe dans la mer, elle devint comme le sang d’un cadavre, et tout ce qui vivait dans la mer mourut.
fr.R: Le deuxième ange a versé sa coupe dans la mer. La mer s’est changée en sang, comme le sang d’un mort. Tous les êtres vivants qui étaient dans la mer sont morts.

sw.L: Na wa pili akalimimina bakuli lake ndani ya bahari, nayo ikawa damu kama [damu] ya mfu, na kila nafsi hai ikafa, vile vilivyo ndani ya bahari.
sw.B: Malaika wa pili alipolimwaga bakuli lake ndani ya bahari, maji yake yakawa kama damu ya maiti, na kila kiumbe kilichoishi baharini kikafa.
sw.R: Malaika wa pili alilimimina bakuli lake baharini. Maji ya bahari yakawa damu, kama damu ya mtu aliyekufa. Kila kiumbe hai kilichokuwa baharini kikafa.

es.L: Y el segundo derramó su copa en el mar, y se convirtió en sangre como de un muerto, y murió todo ser viviente, las cosas que [había] en el mar.
es.B: Cuando el segundo ángel derramó su copa en el mar, este se convirtió en algo como la sangre de un cadáver, y murió todo ser viviente que había en el mar.
es.R: El segundo ángel derramó su copa en el mar. El mar se convirtió en sangre, como la sangre de un muerto. Murieron todos los seres vivos que había en el mar.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: water to blood
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:20-21; compare Revelation 8:8-9, where a third of the sea died). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.
The Greek says "every soul of life", a Hebrew-style way of saying every living creature; "ser viviente" says that in Spanish without suggesting a human soul.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα.

records.literal_gloss: And the third poured out the bowl of him into the rivers and the springs of the waters, and they became blood.

en.L: And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of waters, and they became blood.
en.B: The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and springs, and they turned to blood.
en.R: The third angel poured out his bowl on the rivers and springs. They turned into blood.

fr.L: Et le troisième versa sa coupe dans les fleuves et les sources des eaux, et ils devinrent du sang.
fr.B: Le troisième ange vida sa coupe dans les fleuves et les sources, et ils se changèrent en sang.
fr.R: Le troisième ange a versé sa coupe sur les fleuves et les sources. Ils se sont changés en sang.

sw.L: Na wa tatu akalimimina bakuli lake ndani ya mito na chemchemi za maji, nayo yakawa damu.
sw.B: Malaika wa tatu alilimwaga bakuli lake ndani ya mito na chemchemi za maji, nayo yakageuka kuwa damu.
sw.R: Malaika wa tatu alilimimina bakuli lake juu ya mito na chemchemi. Maji yake yakageuka kuwa damu.

es.L: Y el tercero derramó su copa en los ríos y en los manantiales de las aguas, y se convirtieron en sangre.
es.B: El tercer ángel derramó su copa en los ríos y en los manantiales, y se convirtieron en sangre.
es.R: El tercer ángel derramó su copa en los ríos y en los manantiales. Se convirtieron en sangre.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: the Nile turned to blood
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:19-24; compare 8:10-11). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος· Δίκαιος εἶ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὁ ὅσιος, ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας, ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν, καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς δέδωκας πιεῖν· ἄξιοί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the angel of the waters saying: Righteous you are, the [one] being and the [one who] was, the holy [one], because these things you judged, \v 6 because blood of saints and prophets they poured out, and blood to them you have given to drink; worthy they are.

en.L: And I heard the angel of the waters saying, "Just are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who is and who was, the Holy One, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have judged these things, \v 6 because they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them blood to drink; they deserve it."
en.B: Then I heard the angel of the waters say: "Just are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the one who is and who was, the Holy One, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have judged in this way. \v 6 Because they poured out the blood of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people and prophets, blood is what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them to drink. It is what they have earned."
en.R: Then I heard the angel who is in charge of the waters say, "You are fair in judging this way. You are the Holy One, who is and who always was. \v 6 These people killed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} prophets. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them blood to drink. They deserve it!"

fr.L: Et j’entendis l’ange des eaux qui disait : « Juste es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui es et qui étais, le Saint, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as jugé ces choses, \v 6 parce qu’ils ont versé le sang des saints et des prophètes, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur as donné du sang à boire ; ils [le] méritent. »
fr.B: Puis j’entendis l’ange des eaux dire : « Tu es juste, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui es et qui étais, le Saint, car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as jugé ainsi. \v 6 Parce qu’ils ont versé le sang de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple saint et des prophètes, c’est du sang que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur as donné à boire. Ils l’ont bien mérité. »
fr.R: Puis j’ai entendu l’ange qui s’occupe des eaux dire : « Tu es juste quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juges ainsi. Tu es le Saint, celui qui est et qui a toujours été. \v 6 Ces gens ont tué {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple saint et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} prophètes. Alors {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur as donné du sang à boire. Ils l’ont mérité ! »

sw.L: Nami nikamsikia malaika wa maji akisema, "Wewe u mwenye haki, uliyepo na uliyekuwepo, Mtakatifu, kwa sababu umehukumu mambo haya, \v 6 kwa sababu walimwaga damu ya watakatifu na ya manabii, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} umewapa damu wanywe; wanastahili."
sw.B: Kisha nikamsikia malaika wa maji akisema: "Wewe ni mwenye haki, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyepo na uliyekuwepo, Mtakatifu, kwa kuwa umehukumu hivi. \v 6 Kwa sababu walimwaga damu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} watakatifu na ya manabii, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} umewapa damu wanywe. Hayo ndiyo wanayostahili."
sw.R: Kisha nikamsikia malaika anayeyasimamia maji akisema, "Unahukumu kwa haki unapofanya hivi. Wewe ndiye Mtakatifu, uliyepo na uliyekuwepo daima. \v 6 Watu hawa waliwaua watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na manabii {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. Kwa hiyo umewapa damu wanywe. Wanastahili adhabu hiyo!"

es.L: Y oí al ángel de las aguas que decía: «Justo eres, el que es y el que era, el Santo, porque juzgaste estas cosas, \v 6 porque derramaron sangre de santos y de profetas, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} les has dado a beber sangre; lo merecen».
es.B: Entonces oí que el ángel de las aguas decía: «Justo eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, el que es y el que era, el Santo, porque has juzgado así. \v 6 Ellos derramaron la sangre de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo santo y de los profetas, y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} les has dado a beber sangre. Es lo que merecen».
es.R: Luego oí que el ángel encargado de las aguas decía: «Tú juzgas con justicia al hacer esto. Eres el Santo, el que es y el que siempre ha sido. \v 6 Esta gente mató a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo y a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} profetas. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} les has dado a beber sangre. ¡Se lo merecen!».

decisions.choice: the angel of the waters: the angel set over them
decisions.reason: Revelation speaks of angels with charge over parts of creation, the winds (7:1) and fire (14:18). Jewish writings of the time speak of angels over the waters (1 Enoch 66:2). This one declares God's judgment just, even in his own realm.

decisions.choice: who is and who was: no longer "who is coming"
decisions.reason: As in 11:17, the title lacks "who is coming": God has come in judgment. ὅσιος is the word of 15:4, "holy".

decisions.choice: blood for blood: a just recompense
decisions.reason: Those who poured out the blood of God's people are given blood to drink (compare Isaiah 49:26). The punishment matches the crime; the angel says it is deserved. This answers the martyrs' prayer of 6:10.
As in 5:8.
The angel speaks to God.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); ton peuple saint (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the French term sheet (§9) and the English, which adds "your" at Balanced and Readable; French says "ton peuple saint", with the possessive under the deity_pronoun setting. A "Tu" that begins a sentence is written plainly.
"Haki" is the key term for righteousness and justice in Swahili, so God is called "mwenye haki" (just, righteous) in a judgment that is fair (m3); Readable says he judges "kwa haki".
The settled steps for the holy ones of God, as in 5:8. Balanced and Readable say "your", as the English does, since the angel is speaking to God.

decisions.choice: Justo eres (L); Justo eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} (B); {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} les has dado (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject pronoun unexpressed where the verb shows it; it is written, with its span, where the Greek sets God against the persecutors ("they poured out ... you have given").

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος· Ναί, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the altar saying: Yes, Lord the God the Almighty, true and righteous the judgments of you.

en.L: And I heard the altar saying, "Yes, Lord God the Almighty, true and just [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments."
en.B: Then I heard the altar reply, "Yes, Lord God, the Almighty: {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments are true and right."
en.R: Then I heard the altar say, "Yes, Lord God, the Almighty, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge in a way that is true and fair."

fr.L: Et j’entendis l’autel qui disait : « Oui, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, vrais et justes [sont] {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} jugements. »
fr.B: Puis j’entendis l’autel répondre : « Oui, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} jugements sont vrais et justes. »
fr.R: Puis j’ai entendu l’autel dire : « Oui, Seigneur Dieu, le Tout-Puissant, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} juges d’une manière vraie et juste. »

sw.L: Nami nikasikia madhabahu ikisema, "Ndiyo, Bwana Mungu Mwenyezi, hukumu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} [ni] za kweli na za haki."
sw.B: Kisha nikasikia madhabahu ikijibu: "Ndiyo, Bwana Mungu, Mwenyezi, hukumu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ni za kweli na za haki."
sw.R: Kisha nikasikia madhabahu ikisema, "Ndiyo, Bwana Mungu, Mwenyezi, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unahukumu kwa kweli na kwa haki."

es.L: Y oí al altar que decía: «Sí, Señor Dios Todopoderoso, verdaderos y justos [son] {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} juicios».
es.B: Y oí que el altar respondía: «Sí, Señor Dios Todopoderoso, {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} juicios son verdaderos y justos».
es.R: Luego oí que el altar decía: «Sí, Señor Dios Todopoderoso, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} juzgas con verdad y con justicia».

decisions.choice: the altar speaks: the voice of the prayers and the martyrs
decisions.reason: The souls of the martyrs cried out from under the altar (6:9-10), and the prayers of the saints rose from it (8:3-5). Now the altar agrees that God's judgments are just. The same words return in 19:2.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί.

records.literal_gloss: And the fourth poured out the bowl of him on the sun, and it was given to it to scorch the men with fire.

en.L: And the fourth poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was allowed to scorch {{gender:people|men}} with fire.
en.B: When the fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, it was given power to burn {{gender:people|men}} with fire.
en.R: The fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun. The sun was allowed to burn {{gender:people|men}} with its fire.

fr.L: Et le quatrième versa sa coupe sur le soleil, et il lui fut donné de brûler les {{gender:humains|hommes}} par le feu.
fr.B: Quand le quatrième ange vida sa coupe sur le soleil, celui-ci reçut le pouvoir de brûler les {{gender:gens|hommes}} par le feu.
fr.R: Le quatrième ange a versé sa coupe sur le soleil. Le soleil a pu brûler les {{gender:gens|hommes}} avec son feu.

sw.L: Na wa nne akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya jua, nalo likapewa [ruhusa ya] kuwaunguza watu kwa moto.
sw.B: Malaika wa nne alipolimwaga bakuli lake juu ya jua, jua likapewa uwezo wa kuwaunguza watu kwa moto.
sw.R: Malaika wa nne alilimimina bakuli lake juu ya jua. Jua likaruhusiwa kuwaunguza watu kwa moto wake.

es.L: Y el cuarto derramó su copa sobre el sol, y se le dio [poder] para quemar a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} con fuego.
es.B: Cuando el cuarto ángel derramó su copa sobre el sol, se le dio poder para quemar con fuego a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.
es.R: El cuarto ángel derramó su copa sobre el sol. Se le permitió al sol quemar con su fuego a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}.

decisions.choice: the sun scorches: the reverse of 7:16
decisions.reason: Those who belong to God were promised that the sun would not strike them nor any scorching heat (7:16; Isaiah 49:10). Those who follow the beast are scorched.
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν.

records.literal_gloss: And were scorched the men with heat great, and they blasphemed the name of the God the [one] having the authority over the plagues these, and not they repented to give to him glory.

en.L: And {{gender:people|men}} were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.
en.B: Burned by the fierce heat, {{gender:people|men}} blasphemed the name of the God who had power over these plagues; they would not repent and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.
en.R: The terrible heat burned the {{gender:people|men}}. They said evil things against God, who had power over these plagues. But they would not change their ways and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:humains|hommes}} furent brûlés d’une grande chaleur, et ils blasphémèrent le nom de Dieu, qui a autorité sur ces fléaux, et ils ne se repentirent pas pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donner gloire.
fr.B: Brûlés par une chaleur terrible, les {{gender:gens|hommes}} blasphémèrent le nom du Dieu qui avait pouvoir sur ces fléaux ; ils refusèrent de se repentir et de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendre gloire.
fr.R: La chaleur terrible a brûlé les {{gender:gens|hommes}}. Ils ont dit du mal de Dieu, qui avait le pouvoir sur ces fléaux. Mais ils n’ont pas voulu changer de vie et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendre gloire.

sw.L: Na watu wakaunguzwa kwa joto kuu, nao wakalikufuru jina la Mungu, aliye na mamlaka juu ya mapigo haya, wala hawakutubu ili wampe {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} utukufu.
sw.B: Watu waliunguzwa kwa joto kali, wakalikufuru jina la Mungu aliyekuwa na mamlaka juu ya mapigo haya; hawakukubali kutubu na kumpa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} utukufu.
sw.R: Joto hilo kali liliwaunguza watu. Wakamtukana Mungu, aliyekuwa na uwezo juu ya mapigo hayo. Lakini hawakukubali kuacha dhambi zao na kumpa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} utukufu.

es.L: Y {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} fueron quemados con gran calor, y blasfemaron el nombre de Dios, que tiene autoridad sobre estas plagas, y no se arrepintieron para darle gloria.
es.B: Quemados por el intenso calor, {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} blasfemaron contra el nombre del Dios que tenía poder sobre estas plagas, y no quisieron arrepentirse ni darle gloria.
es.R: El calor terrible quemó a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}. Insultaron a Dios, que tenía poder sobre estas plagas. Pero no quisieron cambiar su manera de vivir ni darle gloria.

decisions.reason: They know that God controls the plagues, yet they curse him instead of turning to him. After the witnesses rose, some gave glory to God (11:13), and the angel called all to give him glory (14:7). Here the hardening is complete, as with Pharaoh (Exodus 9:34-35).

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); changer de vie (R)
decisions.reason: As the French term sheet (§9) and the English Readable "change their ways". The same in 16:11, where Balanced says "se détourner de leurs actes" as the English says "turn from their deeds".

"Kukufuru" is to blaspheme, to speak against God, as settled for the Swahili New Testament; Readable says "kumtukana Mungu" (to insult God), as the English Readable says "said evil things against". "Mapigo" (blows, strokes) is the word for the plagues, as for the plagues of Egypt.
As in 13:5-6: Literal and Balanced keep "blasfemar", Readable says plainly that they insulted God.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου· καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη, καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου, καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And the fifth poured out the bowl of him on the throne of the beast, and became the kingdom of it darkened, and they were gnawing the tongues of them from the pain, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of the heaven from the pains of them and from the sores of them, and not they repented of the works of them.

en.L: And the fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was darkened, and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.
en.B: Then the fifth angel emptied his bowl over the beast's throne, and darkness fell on its kingdom. In their anguish people chewed their tongues, \v 11 and they blasphemed the God of heaven for their pains and their sores; yet they did not turn from their deeds.
en.R: The fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast. Darkness covered its kingdom. People bit their tongues because of the pain. \v 11 They said evil things against the God of heaven because of their pain and their sores. But they would not stop doing evil.

fr.L: Et le cinquième versa sa coupe sur le trône de la bête, et son royaume fut plongé dans les ténèbres, et ils se mordaient la langue de douleur, \v 11 et ils blasphémèrent le Dieu du ciel à cause de leurs douleurs et de leurs ulcères, et ils ne se repentirent pas de leurs œuvres.
fr.B: Puis le cinquième ange vida sa coupe sur le trône de la bête, et les ténèbres s’abattirent sur son royaume. Dans leur angoisse, les gens se mordaient la langue, \v 11 et ils blasphémèrent le Dieu du ciel à cause de leurs souffrances et de leurs ulcères ; mais ils ne se détournèrent pas de leurs actes.
fr.R: Le cinquième ange a versé sa coupe sur le trône de la bête. L’obscurité a couvert son royaume. Les gens se mordaient la langue tant ils avaient mal. \v 11 Ils ont dit du mal du Dieu du ciel à cause de leurs souffrances et de leurs plaies. Mais ils n’ont pas voulu arrêter de faire le mal.

sw.L: Na wa tano akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya kiti cha enzi cha mnyama, na ufalme wake ukatiwa giza, nao wakawa wakiziuma ndimi zao kwa sababu ya maumivu, \v 11 nao wakamkufuru Mungu wa mbinguni kwa sababu ya maumivu yao na kwa sababu ya majipu yao, wala hawakutubu matendo yao.
sw.B: Kisha malaika wa tano akalimwaga bakuli lake juu ya kiti cha enzi cha mnyama, na giza likaufunika ufalme wake. Watu wakaziuma ndimi zao kwa uchungu, \v 11 wakamkufuru Mungu wa mbinguni kwa sababu ya maumivu yao na majipu yao; lakini hawakuyaacha matendo yao.
sw.R: Malaika wa tano alilimimina bakuli lake juu ya kiti cha enzi cha mnyama. Giza likaufunika ufalme wake. Watu wakaziuma ndimi zao kwa sababu ya maumivu. \v 11 Wakamtukana Mungu wa mbinguni kwa sababu ya maumivu yao na majipu yao. Lakini hawakukubali kuacha kutenda maovu.

es.L: Y el quinto derramó su copa sobre el trono de la bestia, y su reino quedó en tinieblas, y se mordían la lengua de dolor, \v 11 y blasfemaron contra el Dios del cielo por sus dolores y por sus llagas, y no se arrepintieron de sus obras.
es.B: El quinto ángel derramó su copa sobre el trono de la bestia, y su reino quedó en tinieblas. La gente se mordía la lengua de dolor, \v 11 y blasfemaban contra el Dios del cielo por sus dolores y sus llagas; pero no se arrepintieron de lo que hacían.
es.R: El quinto ángel derramó su copa sobre el trono de la bestia. La oscuridad cubrió su reino. La gente se mordía la lengua por el dolor. \v 11 Insultaban al Dios del cielo por sus dolores y sus llagas. Pero no quisieron dejar de hacer el mal.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: darkness
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 10:21-23). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: the throne of the beast: the center of its power
decisions.reason: The bowl strikes the seat of the beast's rule, the throne given it by the dragon (13:2). Its kingdom is plunged into darkness.

decisions.choice: their sores: the plagues pile up
decisions.reason: The sores of the first bowl still afflict them: the plagues do not pass but accumulate.
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην· καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου.

records.literal_gloss: And the sixth poured out the bowl of him on the river the great the Euphrates, and was dried up the water of it, so that might be prepared the way of the kings the from rising of sun.

en.L: And the sixth poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared.
en.B: When the sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great river, the Euphrates, its water was dried up so that a road would be ready for the kings from the sunrise.
en.R: The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great Euphrates River. The water in the river dried up. This made a way for the kings from the east to come.

fr.L: Et le sixième versa sa coupe sur le grand fleuve, l’Euphrate, et son eau fut asséchée, afin que soit préparé le chemin des rois [qui viennent] du soleil levant.
fr.B: Quand le sixième ange vida sa coupe sur le grand fleuve, l’Euphrate, son eau tarit, pour que la route soit prête pour les rois venant du soleil levant.
fr.R: Le sixième ange a versé sa coupe sur le grand fleuve Euphrate. L’eau du fleuve a séché. Ainsi, les rois de l’Orient ont eu un chemin pour venir.

sw.L: Na wa sita akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya mto ule mkubwa, Frati, na maji yake yakakauka, ili njia ya wafalme kutoka mawio ya jua iwe tayari.
sw.B: Malaika wa sita alipolimwaga bakuli lake juu ya mto mkubwa, Frati, maji yake yakakauka ili njia iwe tayari kwa ajili ya wafalme wa upande wa mawio ya jua.
sw.R: Malaika wa sita alilimimina bakuli lake juu ya Mto Frati, ule mto mkubwa. Maji ya mto huo yakakauka. Hivyo njia ikawa tayari kwa wafalme kutoka mashariki kuja.

es.L: Y el sexto derramó su copa sobre el gran río Éufrates, y su agua se secó, para que se preparara el camino de los reyes que [vienen] de donde sale el sol.
es.B: Cuando el sexto ángel derramó su copa sobre el gran río Éufrates, sus aguas se secaron para que quedara preparado el camino a los reyes del oriente.
es.R: El sexto ángel derramó su copa sobre el gran río Éufrates. El agua del río se secó. Así quedó abierto el camino para que vinieran los reyes del oriente.

decisions.choice: drying up the Euphrates: a road for invading armies
decisions.reason: God dried up the Red Sea and the Jordan for his people (Exodus 14; Joshua 3), and Isaiah 11:15 speaks of drying up the River. The Greek historian Herodotus tells how Cyrus took Babylon by diverting the Euphrates and marching in along its bed. Here the drying opens a way for kings to come against God's people.

alternatives: the Parthian kings beyond the Euphrates
the kings of the whole world, gathered for the final battle
decisions.reason: In John's day the Parthians beyond the Euphrates were Rome's feared enemy (compare 9:14). In 16:14 the kings of the whole world are gathered for battle. The kings from the east may be part of that gathering, or stand for it.
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.
"Frati" is the usual Swahili name of the Euphrates (m1), with the Greek name of the river behind it.

decisions.choice: de donde sale el sol (L); del oriente (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of the sunrise; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary word for the east.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα τρία ἀκάθαρτα ὡς βάτραχοι·

records.literal_gloss: And I saw out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet spirits three unclean as frogs.

en.L: And I saw [coming] out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet three unclean spirits like frogs.
en.B: And out of the dragon's mouth, the beast's mouth, and the false prophet's mouth I saw three unclean spirits come, like frogs.
en.R: Then I saw three evil spirits that looked like frogs. They came out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.

fr.L: Et je vis [sortir] de la bouche du dragon et de la bouche de la bête et de la bouche du faux prophète trois esprits impurs, comme des grenouilles.
fr.B: Et je vis sortir de la bouche du dragon, de la bouche de la bête et de la bouche du faux prophète trois esprits impurs, semblables à des grenouilles.
fr.R: Puis j’ai vu trois esprits mauvais qui ressemblaient à des grenouilles. Ils sortaient de la bouche du dragon, de la bête et du faux prophète.

sw.L: Na nikaona [wakitoka] katika kinywa cha joka, na katika kinywa cha mnyama, na katika kinywa cha nabii wa uongo, roho wachafu watatu kama vyura.
sw.B: Kisha nikaona roho wachafu watatu wanaofanana na vyura wakitoka katika kinywa cha joka, katika kinywa cha mnyama, na katika kinywa cha nabii wa uongo.
sw.R: Kisha nikaona roho waovu watatu waliofanana na vyura. Walitoka katika vinywa vya yule joka, yule mnyama, na yule nabii wa uongo.

es.L: Y vi [salir] de la boca del dragón, y de la boca de la bestia, y de la boca del falso profeta, tres espíritus impuros como ranas.
es.B: Y vi que de la boca del dragón, de la boca de la bestia y de la boca del falso profeta salían tres espíritus impuros que parecían ranas.
es.R: Luego vi tres espíritus malignos que parecían ranas. Salían de la boca del dragón, de la boca de la bestia y de la boca del falso profeta.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: frogs
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 8:1-15). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: the false prophet: the second beast
decisions.reason: The beast from the earth (13:11-17), who deceives by signs, is now called the false prophet (19:20; 20:10). Dragon, beast and false prophet form a false trinity.

decisions.choice: spirits from their mouths: deceiving words
decisions.reason: The spirits come from their mouths: lies and propaganda that draw the nations to war (16:14). Frogs were unclean animals (Leviticus 11:10-12).
As the French term sheet (§9) at Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the English "evil spirits", since "impur" in this sense is religious language.

decisions.choice: joka; nabii wa uongo; roho wachafu (L, B), roho waovu (R)
decisions.reason: "Joka" (a great serpent, a dragon) for the dragon of chapter 12, and "nabii wa uongo" as in Acts 13:6. Unclean spirits are "roho wachafu" at Literal and Balanced and "roho waovu" at Readable, with the agreement for living beings, as settled in Mark.
The settled pair for unclean spirits in the Gospels, used here too.
The usual Spanish phrase; it names the second beast of chapter 13, as the meaning decision says.

source.text: εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα, ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης.

records.literal_gloss: For they are spirits of demons doing signs, which go out to the kings of the inhabited world whole, to gather them into the war of the day the great of the God the Almighty. \v 15 Behold I am coming as a thief.

en.L: For they are spirits of demons performing signs, which go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the war of the great day of God the Almighty. \v 15 "Look, I am coming like a thief!
en.B: These are spirits of demons, doing signs, and they go out to the kings of all the world to assemble them for war on the great day of God, the Almighty. \v 15 "Look, I come like a thief!
en.R: They are spirits of demons that do miracles, called signs. They go out to the kings of the whole world. They gather the kings together for the battle on the great day of God, the Almighty. \v 15 "Listen! I will come when people do not expect me, like a thief.

fr.L: Car ce sont des esprits de démons qui font des signes, qui s’en vont vers les rois du monde habité tout entier, pour les rassembler pour la guerre du grand jour de Dieu, le Tout-Puissant. \v 15 « Voici, je viens comme un voleur !
fr.B: Ce sont des esprits de démons, qui font des signes ; ils vont trouver les rois du monde entier pour les rassembler en vue de la guerre du grand jour de Dieu, le Tout-Puissant. \v 15 « Voici, je viens comme un voleur !
fr.R: Ce sont des esprits de démons qui font des signes, des choses extraordinaires. Ils vont trouver les rois du monde entier. Ils rassemblent les rois pour la bataille du grand jour de Dieu, le Tout-Puissant. \v 15 « Écoutez ! Je viendrai au moment où l’on ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}attend pas, comme un voleur.

sw.L: Kwa maana hao ni roho wa mapepo wanaofanya ishara, wanaowaendea wafalme wa ulimwengu wote, ili kuwakusanya kwa ajili ya vita vya siku ile kuu ya Mungu Mwenyezi. \v 15 "Tazama, ninakuja kama mwizi!
sw.B: Hao ni roho wa pepo wanaofanya ishara, nao huwaendea wafalme wa dunia nzima ili kuwakusanya kwa ajili ya vita katika siku kuu ya Mungu, Mwenyezi. \v 15 "Tazama, ninakuja kama mwizi!
sw.R: Hao ni roho wa pepo wanaofanya miujiza inayoitwa ishara. Wanawaendea wafalme wa dunia nzima. Wanawakusanya wafalme hao kwa ajili ya vita katika siku ile kuu ya Mungu, Mwenyezi. \v 15 "Sikilizeni! Nitakuja wakati watu wasiponitarajia, kama mwizi.

es.L: Porque son espíritus de demonios que hacen señales, que salen hacia los reyes de todo el mundo habitado, para reunirlos para la guerra del gran día de Dios el Todopoderoso. \v 15 «Mira, vengo como un ladrón.
es.B: Son espíritus de demonios que hacen señales, y salen hacia los reyes de todo el mundo para reunirlos para la guerra del gran día de Dios, el Todopoderoso. \v 15 «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, vengo como un ladrón!
es.R: Son espíritus de demonios que hacen milagros, llamados señales. Van a ver a los reyes de todo el mundo para reunirlos para la batalla del gran día de Dios, el Todopoderoso. \v 15 «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Vendré cuando nadie {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} espere, como viene un ladrón.

decisions.choice: Christ's words break into the vision
decisions.reason: The words "Look, I am coming like a thief" and the blessing that follows (16:15) are spoken by Christ himself, breaking into John's account as a warning to the readers. The SBLGNT sets them apart from the narrative. In the source data the sentence divisions fall so that 16:15 is split across this record and the next; the record follows those divisions.

decisions.choice: the war of the great day of God
decisions.reason: This is the final battle, described in 19:11-21 and 20:7-10. "The great day" recalls "the great day of their wrath" (6:17) and the prophets' day of the LORD.
See the note on 3:3.
As in 13:13.

alternatives: des miracles, qu’on appelle des signes
decisions.reason: As in 13:13: the term sheet never uses "miracle" for sign, so Readable keeps "signes" and says what they were.

alternatives: m’attend with no span, as the English "me"
decisions.reason: Christ speaks of himself; the French style guide (§7) puts the deity_pronoun span on "me", "m’" in his words, though the English "me" has none. "Je" takes no span.

Christ's words break into the vision and are spoken to all readers, so Balanced and Readable use the plural, as "idou" said to a group is rendered in 1:7; Literal keeps the bare "Mira" of the Greek form.

source.text: μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρμαγεδών.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the [one] watching and keeping the garments of him, so that not naked he walks and they see the shame of him. \v 16 And he gathered them into the place the [one] being called in Hebrew Armageddon.

en.L: Blessed [is] the one who stays awake and keeps {{gender:their|his}} garments, so that {{gender:they may|he may}} not walk naked and people see {{gender:their|his}} shame." \v 16 And [the spirits] gathered them to the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.
en.B: How blessed is anyone who keeps watch and holds on to {{gender:their|his}} clothes, and so will not walk about naked with {{gender:their|his}} shame on view!" \v 16 And the spirits brought the kings together at the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.
en.R: God blesses the person who stays awake and keeps {{gender:their|his}} clothes on. Then {{gender:they|he}} will not have to walk around naked and be ashamed." \v 16 Then the spirits gathered the kings together at the place called Armageddon in the Hebrew language.

fr.L: Heureux celui qui veille et qui garde ses vêtements, afin de ne pas marcher nu et qu’on ne voie pas sa honte. » \v 16 Et [les esprits] les rassemblèrent au lieu appelé en hébreu Harmaguédon.
fr.B: Heureux celui qui veille et qui garde ses vêtements, pour ne pas aller nu en laissant voir sa honte ! » \v 16 Et les esprits rassemblèrent les rois au lieu appelé en hébreu Harmaguédon.
fr.R: Dieu bénit celui qui reste éveillé et garde ses vêtements sur lui. Il n’aura pas à se promener tout nu et à avoir honte. » \v 16 Puis les esprits ont rassemblé les rois à l’endroit qu’on appelle Harmaguédon en hébreu.

sw.L: Heri aliye macho na kuyatunza mavazi yake, ili asitembee uchi na watu wakaiona aibu yake." \v 16 Na [roho hao] wakawakusanya mahali paitwapo kwa Kiebrania Armagedoni.
sw.B: Heri mtu anayekesha na kuyashika mavazi yake, ili asitembee uchi, aibu yake ikaonekana!" \v 16 Kisha roho hao wakawakusanya wafalme mahali paitwapo kwa Kiebrania Armagedoni.
sw.R: Mungu humbariki mtu anayekaa macho na kuvaa mavazi yake. Hatatembea uchi na kuona aibu." \v 16 Kisha roho hao wakawakusanya wafalme mahali paitwapo Armagedoni kwa lugha ya Kiebrania.

es.L: Dichoso el que vela y guarda su ropa, para que no ande desnudo y vean su vergüenza». \v 16 Y [los espíritus] los reunieron en el lugar que en hebreo se llama Armagedón.
es.B: ¡Qué dichoso es el que se mantiene despierto y guarda su ropa, para no andar desnudo y que todos vean su vergüenza!». \v 16 Y los espíritus reunieron a los reyes en el lugar que en hebreo se llama Armagedón.
es.R: Dios bendice al que se mantiene despierto y tiene su ropa puesta. Así no tendrá que andar desnudo ni pasar vergüenza». \v 16 Luego los espíritus reunieron a los reyes en el lugar que en el idioma hebreo se llama Armagedón.

decisions.choice: the third blessing: staying awake and clothed
decisions.reason: This is the third of the book's seven blessings (1:3). Staying awake and keeping one's clothes means remaining faithful and ready (3:2-4, 18). To be found naked is to be put to shame at his coming.

alternatives: a real place where the final battle will be fought
a symbol of the final gathering of the nations against God
decisions.reason: The name is most likely Hebrew "Har Megiddo", "mountain of Megiddo". Megiddo overlooked a plain where famous battles were fought (Judges 5:19; 2 Kings 23:29; compare Zechariah 12:11), but there is no mountain of that name. The name may be a symbol for the place where the nations gather against God and are defeated.

decisions.choice: he gathered: the spirits are the subject
decisions.reason: συνήγαγεν is singular, but its subject is most likely the spirits of 16:13-14; a neuter plural subject in Greek can take a singular verb.
Balanced and Readable name the subject and the object (m3).

decisions.choice: "celui qui … ses vêtements … sa honte", "il" with no gender span
alternatives: "la personne … elle" with a gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English needs {{gender:their|his}} and {{gender:they|he}}, French "celui qui" is generic and its possessives say nothing about sex, so the French style guide (§7) adds no span.
"Harmaguédon" is the usual French spelling of the name and keeps its first syllable, "mountain" (m2); "Armageddon" is the English form.
The place name in its familiar Swahili form; the meaning decision explains that it is the mountain of Megiddo (m2).

alternatives: a gender span, as in the English
decisions.reason: The Swahili possessive "yake" means his or her and the verb prefix "a-" he or she, so the English spans "their|his" have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: el que vela ... desnudo (no gender span)
decisions.reason: Spanish "el que" and "desnudo" are the generic forms and include women, as in 3:5 and 14:9, so the English gender span on "their/his" has no Spanish counterpart.
The usual Spanish spelling of the name; the meaning decision explains that it points to the hill of Megiddo.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα· Γέγονεν καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί, καὶ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφ’ οὗ ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας, καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη, καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν· καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And the seventh poured out the bowl of him on the air, and came out a voice great out of the temple from the throne saying: It has happened. \v 18 And there were lightnings and voices and thunders, and earthquake happened great, such as not happened since men came to be on the earth, so great earthquake so mighty, \v 19 and became the city the great into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before the God to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of the wrath of him;

en.L: And the seventh poured out his bowl on the air, and a loud voice came out of the temple, from the throne, saying, "It is done!" \v 18 And there were lightnings and voices and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as had not happened since {{gender:people|men}} came to be on the earth, so great an earthquake, so mighty, \v 19 and the great city split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell, and Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath.
en.B: When the seventh angel emptied his bowl into the air, a great voice came out of the temple, from the throne: "It is done!" \v 18 Lightning, loud sounds, and thunder followed, and an earthquake struck so violent that nothing like it had ever happened since human beings first lived on the earth. \v 19 The great city was torn into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the great was not forgotten before God: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made her drink the cup of the wine of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} raging anger.
en.R: The seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air. A loud voice came from the throne in the temple. It said, "It is finished!" \v 18 There was lightning, loud noise, and thunder. And there was a terrible earthquake, the worst since people have lived on the earth. \v 19 The great city split into three parts. The cities of the nations fell down. And God remembered Babylon the great city. He made her drink from the cup filled with the wine of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} terrible anger.

fr.L: Et le septième versa sa coupe dans l’air, et une voix forte sortit du temple, du trône, disant : « C’est fait ! » \v 18 Et il y eut des éclairs, et des voix, et des tonnerres, et il y eut un grand tremblement de terre, tel qu’il n’y en avait pas eu depuis que les {{gender:humains|hommes}} sont sur la terre, un tremblement de terre si grand, si violent, \v 19 et la grande ville se divisa en trois parties, et les villes des nations tombèrent, et Babylone la grande fut rappelée au souvenir devant Dieu, pour lui donner la coupe du vin de la fureur de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère.
fr.B: Quand le septième ange vida sa coupe dans l’air, une voix forte sortit du temple, venant du trône : « C’est fait ! » \v 18 Il y eut des éclairs, des fracas et des coups de tonnerre, et un tremblement de terre si violent qu’il n’y en avait jamais eu de pareil depuis que les êtres humains vivent sur la terre. \v 19 La grande ville se fendit en trois parties, et les villes des nations s’écroulèrent. Dieu n’oublia pas Babylone la grande : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui fit boire la coupe du vin de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ardente.
fr.R: Le septième ange a versé sa coupe dans l’air. Une voix forte est venue du trône, dans le temple. Elle a dit : « C’est fini ! » \v 18 Il y a eu des éclairs, de grands bruits et du tonnerre. Et il y a eu un terrible tremblement de terre, le pire depuis que les gens vivent sur la terre. \v 19 La grande ville s’est fendue en trois parties. Les villes des nations se sont écroulées. Et Dieu s’est souvenu de Babylone la grande ville. Il lui a fait boire la coupe remplie du vin de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} terrible colère.

sw.L: Na wa saba akalimimina bakuli lake juu ya anga, na sauti kubwa ikatoka katika hekalu, kutoka kwenye kiti cha enzi, ikisema, "Imekwisha kuwa!" \v 18 Na kukawa na umeme wa radi na sauti na ngurumo, na kukawa na tetemeko kuu la nchi, ambalo halijawahi kutokea tangu wanadamu walipokuwa juu ya dunia, tetemeko kubwa namna hiyo, kuu hivyo, \v 19 na mji ule mkubwa ukagawanyika sehemu tatu, na miji ya mataifa ikaanguka, na Babeli mkuu akakumbukwa mbele za Mungu, ili ampe kikombe cha divai ya hasira kali ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Malaika wa saba alipolimwaga bakuli lake angani, sauti kubwa ikatoka hekaluni, kutoka kwenye kiti cha enzi, ikisema: "Imekwisha!" \v 18 Kukawa na umeme wa radi, sauti kubwa na ngurumo, na tetemeko la nchi likatokea, kubwa mno kiasi kwamba halijawahi kutokea kama hilo tangu wanadamu walipoanza kuishi duniani. \v 19 Mji ule mkubwa ukapasuka sehemu tatu, na miji ya mataifa ikaanguka. Mungu hakumsahau Babeli mkuu: alimnywesha kikombe cha divai ya hasira kali ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Malaika wa saba alilimimina bakuli lake angani. Sauti kubwa ikatoka kwenye kiti cha enzi kilichokuwa hekaluni. Ilisema, "Yote yamekamilika!" \v 18 Kukawa na umeme wa radi, kelele kubwa na ngurumo. Kukawa pia na tetemeko kubwa la nchi, baya kuliko yote tangu wanadamu waanze kuishi duniani. \v 19 Mji ule mkubwa ukagawanyika sehemu tatu. Miji ya mataifa ikaanguka. Mungu akaukumbuka Babeli, ule mji mkubwa. Alimnywesha kikombe kilichojaa divai ya hasira kali ya ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

es.L: Y el séptimo derramó su copa sobre el aire, y salió una gran voz del templo, desde el trono, que decía: «Hecho está». \v 18 Y hubo relámpagos y voces y truenos, y hubo un gran terremoto, como no lo hubo desde que {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} existen sobre la tierra, un terremoto tan grande, tan fuerte, \v 19 y la gran ciudad se partió en tres partes, y las ciudades de las naciones cayeron, y Babilonia la grande fue recordada delante de Dios, para darle la copa del vino del furor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira.
es.B: Cuando el séptimo ángel derramó su copa en el aire, del templo salió una gran voz que venía del trono: «¡Ya está hecho!». \v 18 Hubo relámpagos, estruendos y truenos, y un terremoto tan violento como no lo había habido jamás desde que hay seres humanos sobre la tierra. \v 19 La gran ciudad se partió en tres partes, y las ciudades de las naciones se derrumbaron. Dios no se olvidó de Babilonia la grande: le dio a beber la copa del vino de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ardiente ira.
es.R: El séptimo ángel derramó su copa en el aire. Del trono que está en el templo salió una voz fuerte que dijo: «¡Todo ha terminado!». \v 18 Hubo relámpagos, ruidos fuertes y truenos. Y hubo un terremoto terrible, el peor desde que hay gente en la tierra. \v 19 La gran ciudad se partió en tres partes. Las ciudades de las naciones se derrumbaron. Y Dios se acordó de Babilonia la gran ciudad. La hizo beber de la copa llena del vino de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} terrible ira.

decisions.choice: It is done: the last plague completes God's wrath
decisions.reason: Γέγονεν is perfect: it has happened and stands done. The voice from the throne declares the end of the series (15:1). The same word sounds again in 21:6, at the making of all things new.

decisions.choice: an earthquake like none before: Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of "a time of trouble such as never has been since there was a nation" (Daniel 12:1; compare Mark 13:19). The signs of God's presence (4:5; 8:5; 11:19) reach their height.
The great city is named in the same sentence: Babylon the great (compare 14:8; 17:18; 18:10). Its fall is told in chapters 17-18.

decisions.choice: remembered before God: God does not forget her sins
decisions.reason: To be remembered before God is to have one's deeds brought into judgment (18:5). The cup is the cup of 14:10; "the fury of his wrath" doubles the word for anger, as in 19:15.
The verb means to pour out; Balanced varies it with "emptied" to avoid repeating the same phrase seven times.

"Babeli" is the Swahili name of Babylon, as in 1 Peter 5:13. The city is a woman in these chapters, so Balanced and Readable say "alimnywesha" (made her drink); Swahili "-m-" covers her without a gendered pronoun.

The Greek perfect says that what was to happen has now happened (m1); Literal "imekwisha kuwa" keeps "it has come to be", Balanced the short cry "Imekwisha!" (it is done), Readable "everything is complete", as the English Readable says "It is finished".

decisions.choice: Hecho está (L); ¡Ya está hecho! (B); ¡Todo ha terminado! (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect says the thing is accomplished and stands so; Spanish says it in a short cry at each level.
The English has a gender span; Spanish "seres humanos" suits the phrase about humankind first living on the earth.

source.text: καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν, καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And every island fled, and mountains not were found.

en.L: And every island fled, and mountains were not found.
en.B: Every island ran away, and the mountains were found no more.
en.R: Every island disappeared, and the mountains could not be found.

fr.L: Et toute île s’enfuit, et les montagnes ne furent pas retrouvées.
fr.B: Toutes les îles s’enfuirent, et l’on ne trouva plus de montagnes.
fr.R: Toutes les îles ont disparu, et on ne pouvait plus trouver les montagnes.

sw.L: Na kila kisiwa kikakimbia, na milima haikuonekana.
sw.B: Kila kisiwa kikakimbia, na milima haikuonekana tena.
sw.R: Kila kisiwa kikatoweka, na milima haikuweza kuonekana tena.

es.L: Y toda isla huyó, y no se hallaron montes.
es.B: Todas las islas huyeron, y los montes desaparecieron.
es.R: Todas las islas desaparecieron, y no se podían encontrar los montes.

decisions.choice: islands and mountains gone: the world's foundations shaken
decisions.reason: In 6:14 they were moved from their places; here they vanish (compare 20:11, where earth and sky flee from God's presence).

source.text: καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And hail great as talent-weight comes down out of the heaven on the men, and blasphemed the men the God because of the plague of the hail, because great is the plague of it exceedingly.

en.L: And great hail, about a talent in weight, comes down from heaven on {{gender:people|men}}, and {{gender:people|men}} blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great.
en.B: Hailstones weighing about {{units:seventy-five pounds|a talent}} each came down out of the sky on {{gender:people|men}}, and they blasphemed God over the plague of hail, because the plague of it was very severe.
en.R: Huge hailstones fell from the sky on {{gender:people|men}}. Each one weighed about {{units:seventy-five pounds|a talent}}. People said evil things against God because the hail was so terrible.

fr.L: Et une grosse grêle, du poids d’un talent, descend du ciel sur les {{gender:humains|hommes}}, et les {{gender:humains|hommes}} blasphémèrent Dieu à cause du fléau de la grêle, car son fléau est extrêmement grand.
fr.B: Des grêlons pesant {{units:environ 35 kilos|un talent}} chacun tombèrent du ciel sur les {{gender:gens|hommes}}, et ils blasphémèrent Dieu à cause du fléau de la grêle, car ce fléau était terrible.
fr.R: D’énormes grêlons sont tombés du ciel sur les {{gender:gens|hommes}}. Chacun pesait {{units:environ 35 kilos|un talent}}. Les gens ont dit du mal de Dieu parce que la grêle était terrible.

sw.L: Na mvua ya mawe kubwa, [kila jiwe] kama talanta [kwa uzito], inashuka kutoka mbinguni juu ya watu, na watu wakamkufuru Mungu kwa sababu ya pigo la mvua ya mawe, kwa maana pigo lake ni kubwa mno.
sw.B: Mvua kubwa ya mawe, kila jiwe likiwa na uzito wa kama {{units:kilo 34|talanta moja}}, ikawashukia watu kutoka angani, nao wakamkufuru Mungu kwa sababu ya pigo hilo la mvua ya mawe, kwa kuwa pigo hilo lilikuwa kali mno.
sw.R: Mawe makubwa ya mvua yakaanguka kutoka angani juu ya watu. Kila jiwe lilikuwa na uzito wa kama {{units:kilo 34|talanta moja}}. Watu wakamtukana Mungu kwa sababu mvua hiyo ya mawe ilikuwa mbaya sana.

es.L: Y un gran granizo, como de un talento de peso, baja del cielo sobre {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}; y {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} blasfemaron contra Dios por la plaga del granizo, porque su plaga es sumamente grande.
es.B: Del cielo cayeron sobre {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} enormes granizos de {{units:unos 34 kilos|un talento}} cada uno, y ellos blasfemaron contra Dios por la plaga del granizo, porque era una plaga terrible.
es.R: Cayeron del cielo enormes granizos sobre {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}. Cada uno pesaba {{units:unos 34 kilos|un talento}}. La gente insultó a Dios porque el granizo era terrible.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: hail
decisions.reason: Like the trumpets, the bowls recall the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 9:22-26; compare Joshua 10:11). The bowls strike the whole of each realm, not a third: these are the last plagues (15:1).

decisions.choice: a talent: a very heavy weight
decisions.reason: A talent was the largest unit of weight, varying by region from about 55 to 100 pounds (25 to 45 kilograms). Hailstones of that size would crush whatever they struck.
As after the fourth and fifth bowls (16:9, 11), people blaspheme God instead of repenting.
Literal keeps the Greek measure; Balanced and Readable give a modern equivalent, with the original as the alternative (m2).

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 35 kilos|un talent}} (B, R); "du poids d’un talent" (L)
decisions.reason: French uses metric measures by default (style guide §7), where the English has US pounds; a talent weighed about 34 kilograms. Literal keeps the Greek measure.

As the Swahili style guide sets for units: metric by default (a talent weighed about 34 kilograms), with the original measure as the alternative, where the English default is seventy-five pounds. Literal keeps "talanta".
Spanish gives the metric equivalent of the English "seventy-five pounds", rounded; the original unit is the alternative, and Literal keeps it.
Literal keeps the Greek present tense, as elsewhere in the book.
